claim: Currently, you can connect one Amazon Managed Grafana workspace to one VPC endpoint in the same Region and same account. To reach VPCs in other Regions or accounts, you can use VPC peering or AWS Transit Gateway.

values.display: Virtual Private Cloud peering or AWS Transit Gateway

However, you can use Virtual Private Cloud peering or AWS Transit Gateway to connect the cross-region or cross-account VPCs, then connect the select the VPC endpoint that’s in the same account and same region as your Amazon Managed Grafana workspace.

claim: Amazon Managed Grafana supports two modes for user and host access of a workspace: open access and restricted access. Open access is the default when no VPC endpoints or managed prefix list restrictions limit access to the workspace URL, and users must still authenticate with the configured identity provider.
question: Is my Amazon Managed Grafana workspace URL publicly reachable?

values.display: open access mode is the default access setting

evidence.quote: Amazon Managed Grafana supports two modes for user and host access of your Grafana workspace: open access and restricted access. The open access mode is the default access setting for Grafana workspaces when there are no VPC endpoints or managed prefix list restrictions to reach your Grafana workspace URL; however, users must still authenticate with the configured identity provider(s) in order to log in to the workspace.

claim: The restricted access mode lets you specify the inbound network traffic that is allowed to reach your workspace. To restrict access, you can configure prefix lists to specify the IP address ranges from which users and hosts can reach it.
question: How do I restrict access to an Amazon Managed Grafana workspace?

evidence.quote: The restricted access mode enables you to specify the inbound network traffic that is allowed to reach your workspace. To restrict access, you can configure prefix lists to specify IP address ranges from which users and hosts can reach your Grafana workspace.
